clinician.trajectory_summary: A 64-year-old male with a 20 pack-year smoking history presented with nausea, vomiting, and euvolemic hyponatremia suggestive of paraneoplastic syndrome. Initial chest X-ray was negative but physical exam noted mild right upper lung wheezing. Chest CT revealed a 3.0 × 1.9 cm conglomerate of nodules in the right upper lobe with ipsilateral mediastinal lymphadenopathy. Bronchoscopic biopsy showed positive immunostaining for neuroendocrine markers consistent with small cell lung cancer. A PET scan performed post-discharge confirmed mediastinal lymph node uptake, leading to classification as limited stage small cell lung cancer. The patient was started on chemotherapy with planned prophylactic cranial irradiation.
